name: Karna Poorana (ear oil therapy)
seo_title: Karna Poorana Ear Oil Therapy in Patna | Sabka Ved
meta_description: Karna poorana fills the ear with warm medicated oil for a set time. Classical roots, who it may suit, strict cautions on ear infection, and our Patna method.
summary: Karna poorana is a classical Ayurvedic therapy in which lukewarm medicated oil is gently filled into the ear canal and held for a set time while the patient lies on their side. It is used for dryness, vata-type ear discomfort and as part of care for some head and neck complaints, but only after the ear has been examined and infection or a perforated eardrum ruled out.

at_a_glance.typical_session: 15 to 30 minutes for both ears (decided after assessment)
at_a_glance.supervision: Therapist with doctor oversight, after ear examination

body_html:
In many Indian homes, a grandmother's answer to an earache or a winter wind is a few warm drops of mustard oil with garlic. Doctors today rightly worry about that habit, because oil in an infected ear or behind a torn eardrum can do harm. Yet the classical texts of Ayurveda did describe oiling the ears as part of a healthy routine, and as a treatment for particular complaints. Karna poorana is the clinical form of that idea, and the difference between the clinic and the kitchen lies in one essential step: examining the ear first.

What Karna Poorana means

Karna is the ear and poorana means filling. In Karna poorana, the ear canal is filled with lukewarm medicated oil, or occasionally another medicated liquid, and the oil is held there for a fixed time while the patient lies on one side. The outer ear and the area around it are usually massaged gently before and after.

A related, milder practice is karna taila, putting just a few drops of oil into the ears as part of the daily routine.

Classical background

Charaka Samhita, in the Sutrasthana chapter on daily regimen, recommends daily filling of the ears with oil and describes its benefits in traditional terms: it is said to prevent ear disorders caused by vata, stiffness of the neck and jaw, hardness of hearing and deafness. Ashtanga Hridaya (around 7th century CE) repeats this within dinacharya. Sushruta Samhita, as the surgical classic, discusses ear diseases (karna roga) and their treatments, including the use of medicated oils and the timing of holding them in the ear, often expressed in terms of matra, a traditional unit of time.

Karna poorana is therefore a classical procedure. In modern Ayurvedic practice it falls under Shalakya Tantra, the branch dealing with the eyes, ears, nose, throat and head.

How it is understood to work, and what research shows

The classical view

The ear is described as a seat of vata, and the sense of hearing as linked with akasha, space. Dryness, ringing, a blocked feeling, itching in a dry canal and some forms of age-related hearing difficulty are read as vata disturbances. Warm, unctuous oil counters dryness and is believed to calm vata in the ear and the surrounding region, including the jaw and neck.

What modern research says

Evidence is limited. A 2013 case discussion in the Journal of Ayurveda and Integrative Medicine described Ayurvedic management of presbycusis (age-related hearing loss) that included local therapies, and a 2024 protocol in JMIR Research Protocols (Project TOPMAC) sets out an exploratory randomised trial of Ayurvedic management of presbycusis. Results of that trial are not yet established. In conventional medicine, oil drops are sometimes used to soften ear wax, but oil is avoided in infections and perforations. We therefore describe Karna poorana as a traditional supportive therapy, not a treatment that restores hearing.

Who may benefit

  • Dry, itchy ear canals without infection
  • A feeling of fullness or mild discomfort in the ears linked with dryness or cold wind, after examination
  • Some patients with tinnitus or age-related hearing changes, as one part of a plan alongside an ENT evaluation
  • Jaw and neck tension, combined with local massage
  • As part of a broader head and neck therapy plan, for example with nasya

Strict contraindications

  • Any ear discharge, pus, bleeding or foul smell
  • Known or suspected perforated eardrum, grommets or ear tubes
  • Recent ear surgery
  • Ear pain with fever, swelling behind the ear or severe pain, which need urgent ENT care
  • Fungal infection of the ear canal
  • Sudden hearing loss or sudden vertigo: these are urgent medical conditions
  • Acute cold, sinusitis and nasal congestion, in many cases

Karna poorana is never a replacement for an ENT examination. Please do not put oil, garlic or any other remedy into an ear that is painful, discharging or suddenly not hearing. Continue any treatment your doctor prescribes.

Karna Poorana at Sabka Ved Wellness

Examination first

Dr. Aditya Kunal asks about ear pain, discharge, past infections, ear surgery, hearing changes and ringing, and examines the ear. If there is any sign of infection, a perforation or a condition that needs ENT care, Karna poorana is not done and you are advised accordingly. Hearing loss and tinnitus are best evaluated by an ENT specialist with audiometry before any Ayurvedic plan is made.

Preparation

A classical medicated oil, chosen for your complaint, is warmed in a water bath to body temperature. The temperature is checked carefully, because the ear canal is sensitive and hot oil can burn.

The procedure, for understanding

  1. The area around the ear, the neck and the jaw is gently massaged with warm oil, sometimes followed by mild local warmth.
  2. You lie on your side with the ear to be treated facing up.
  3. The lukewarm oil is poured slowly into the ear canal, filling it without force.
  4. The oil is held for the set time while the area around the ear is massaged lightly.
  5. You turn to let the oil drain into a clean cotton pad, and the outer ear is wiped dry.
  6. The process is repeated for the other ear.

Hearing may feel muffled while the oil is in the ear, which is expected. Tell the therapist immediately if you feel pain, dizziness or burning.

Aftercare

Keep the ears protected from cold wind and water for some time afterwards. A light cotton plug may be suggested. Avoid inserting cotton buds deep into the ear, a habit that pushes wax inward and can injure the canal. Avoid very loud sound exposure during the course.

Why it costs what it does

Karna poorana is a short therapy, so its cost is modest. You are paying for a suitable classical oil, careful warming and temperature checks, therapist time for massage and the procedure on both ears, clean disposables and linen, and most importantly the doctor's examination that makes it safe. Fixed prices are not published because plans differ.

Earphones, traffic and modern ears

Ayurveda listed loud noise and cold wind among the causes of ear disorders, long before earphones existed. Today many young people in Patna spend hours a day with earphones at high volume, ride through heavy traffic noise and sit in air-conditioned rooms with cold air blowing at the head. Practical advice often matters more than any therapy: keep earphone volume low, take breaks, use over-ear headphones rather than in-ear buds when possible, cover your ears on winter rides and avoid swimming in dirty water. If you notice ringing that does not go away, a persistent blocked feeling or any reduction in hearing, get an ENT examination and a hearing test first.

The cotton bud habit

Many patients who come with itchy or blocked ears turn out to be cleaning them daily with cotton buds, hairpins or matchsticks. The ear canal cleans itself, and wax is protective. Digging inside removes the protective layer, irritates the skin and pushes wax deeper. If you feel blocked, have the ear examined rather than digging or putting in oil yourself.

faqs: Karna poorana is a classical Ayurvedic therapy in which lukewarm medicated oil is filled into the ear canal and held for a set time while you lie on your side.
Is it safe to put oil in the ears?
Only in a healthy ear that has been examined. Oil must never be put into an ear with discharge, pain with fever, a perforated eardrum, grommets or recent surgery.
Can Karna Poorana cure hearing loss or tinnitus?
No. It may be used as supportive care, but hearing loss and tinnitus need an ENT evaluation, and research on Karna poorana for these conditions is still at an early stage.
What does Karna Poorana feel like?
Warm and muffled. Hearing is temporarily dulled while the oil is in the ear. Pain, dizziness or burning should be reported immediately.
Can I do Karna Poorana at home?
A few drops of oil as a daily routine may be suggested for healthy ears, but full Karna poorana should be done after examination at the clinic.
